terms.plain: Your total assets minus total liabilities. The bottom-line measure of your financial position.
terms.more: Negative net worth means you owe more than you own; positive means you have a cushion.

terms.plain: The movement of money in and out of your accounts over time. Positive cash flow means more money coming in than going out.
terms.more: Essential to solvency; even high net worth can fail with poor cash flow.

terms.plain: A spending plan that allocates money to different categories based on expected income and goals.
terms.more: Not a restriction—a tool to align spending with priorities.

terms.plain: A method where you allocate a fixed amount to each spending category (like cash envelopes), and stop spending once it runs out.
terms.more: Forces awareness and prevents overspending in any one category.

terms.plain: Cash savings set aside to cover unexpected expenses (3-6 months of living costs).
terms.more: Prevents debt spirals when emergencies strike; foundational financial security.

terms.plain: Financial Independence, Retire Early. A movement focused on maximizing savings rate to retire before traditional age.
terms.more: Requires 25-30x annual expenses in invested assets for safe withdrawal.

terms.plain: A tax-advantaged retirement account where you contribute after-tax money and withdrawals in retirement are tax-free.
terms.more: No required minimum distributions; great for long-term wealth building.

terms.plain: An employer-sponsored retirement plan where contributions reduce your current taxable income.
terms.more: Employer match is free money; always contribute enough to capture it.

terms.plain: The annual percentage of a fund's assets paid to cover operating costs and management fees.
terms.more: Low expense ratios (under 0.2%) significantly boost long-term returns.

terms.plain: APR (Annual Percentage Rate) is interest without compounding; APY includes the effect of compounding over a year.
terms.more: APY is always higher; critical for savings and debt decisions.

terms.plain: Total monthly debt payments divided by gross monthly income. Lenders use this to assess lending risk.
terms.more: Lower is better; below 36% is typically considered healthy.

terms.plain: The process of paying off a loan through regular installments that cover both principal and interest.
terms.more: Early payments mostly cover interest; later payments mostly cover principal.

terms.plain: The breakdown of your investments across stocks, bonds, cash, and other asset classes based on risk tolerance and goals.
terms.more: More important than picking individual securities for long-term wealth.

terms.plain: A statistical method that runs thousands of scenarios with random market outcomes to estimate the probability of financial goals succeeding.
terms.more: Reveals true retirement safety, not just average-case analysis.

terms.plain: The original purchase price of an investment, used to calculate capital gains or losses when sold.
terms.more: Essential for tax planning and determining actual profit.

terms.plain: Profit from selling an investment for more than its cost basis. Taxed differently than regular income.
terms.more: Long-term gains (1+ year) are taxed lower than short-term gains.

terms.plain: The range of income at which a specific tax rate applies. The US uses a progressive system with multiple brackets.
terms.more: Moving into a higher bracket only increases tax on income within that bracket.

terms.plain: Marginal rate is the tax on the next dollar earned; effective rate is total tax divided by total income.
terms.more: Your marginal rate drives financial decisions; your effective rate shows overall tax burden.

terms.plain: Interest earned on both the principal and previously earned interest, creating exponential growth.
terms.more: The eighth wonder of the world; time is your greatest asset.

terms.plain: Spreading investments across different asset classes, sectors, and geographies to reduce risk.
terms.more: Uncorrelated assets protect you when one market struggles.

terms.plain: How quickly an asset can be converted to cash without significant loss of value.
terms.more: Cash is most liquid; real estate and collectibles are least liquid.

terms.plain: Investing a fixed amount at regular intervals, regardless of asset price, to reduce impact of market volatility.
terms.more: Removes emotion and timing risk from investing.

terms.plain: Periodically adjusting your portfolio back to target allocations to maintain risk level and enforce buy-low/sell-high.
terms.more: Annual or quarterly rebalancing keeps discipline in check.

terms.plain: The percentage of income you save rather than spend. Critical for wealth building and achieving financial independence.
terms.more: Doubling your savings rate cuts time to financial goals by 50%+.

terms.plain: Money already spent that cannot be recovered. Should never influence future financial decisions.
terms.more: Ignore sunk costs; decide based only on future value and opportunity.

terms.plain: The benefit forgone by choosing one option over the next best alternative.
terms.more: Critical for deciding where to allocate time, money, and attention.

terms.plain: Your ability and willingness to endure investment losses without panic-selling or deviating from your plan.
terms.more: Determine this honestly; it drives your entire investment strategy.

terms.plain: A decline of 10% or more from recent highs, commonly occurring several times per decade.
terms.more: Normal and necessary; panic-selling locks in losses.

terms.plain: A prolonged decline of 20%+ from recent highs, often accompanied by economic recession.
terms.more: Happens roughly every 3-5 years; wealth is built by staying invested.

terms.plain: An extended period of rising prices and investor optimism, often gaining 20%+ or more.
terms.more: Can last years; missing just 10 best days cuts returns by 50%.

terms.plain: The general increase in prices of goods and services over time, reducing purchasing power.
terms.more: Erodes cash savings; invest to stay ahead of inflation.

terms.plain: Your investment return minus inflation. The true measure of wealth growth.
terms.more: 5% nominal return minus 2% inflation = 3% real return.

terms.plain: A fund that tracks a market index (like the S&P 500) with low fees and automatic diversification.
terms.more: Outperforms 80%+ of actively managed funds over 15+ years.

terms.plain: A fund traded like a stock that holds a basket of securities, offering low cost and tax efficiency.
terms.more: Often preferable to mutual funds for individual investors.

terms.plain: A portion of company profits distributed to shareholders, usually quarterly.
terms.more: Provides passive income and can compound significantly over decades.

terms.plain: Stock price divided by earnings per share; indicates if a stock is expensive or cheap relative to profits.
terms.more: Lower P/E can signal undervalue; context matters greatly.

terms.plain: A numerical rating (300-850) based on credit history, used by lenders to assess default risk.
terms.more: Each 50-point increase saves thousands in interest over a lifetime.

terms.plain: The percentage of available credit you're using. Keeping it under 30% is best for credit score.
terms.more: Even zero balance is better than high utilization.

terms.plain: Methods like debt snowball (smallest first) or avalanche (highest rate first) to systematically eliminate debt.
terms.more: Snowball provides psychological wins; avalanche minimizes interest.

terms.plain: A long-term loan to purchase real estate, secured by the property itself.
terms.more: 30-year fixed is common; prepaying principal accelerates payoff.

terms.plain: In real estate, the difference between property value and outstanding mortgage. Your true ownership stake.
terms.more: Building equity through payments and appreciation is core wealth strategy.

terms.plain: For banks and lenders, the profit on interest charged versus interest paid to depositors.
terms.more: Affects rate offers you'll receive on deposits and loans.

terms.plain: Two consecutive quarters of negative GDP growth, typically marked by job losses and reduced spending.
terms.more: Happens every 5-10 years on average; stay employed and invested.

terms.plain: When income growth fails to keep pace with inflation, reducing real purchasing power.
terms.more: One reason to maximize savings rate and invest for compounding.

terms.plain: When passive income and assets cover living expenses, eliminating the need to work for money.
terms.more: Earlier than retirement; the ultimate financial goal.

terms.plain: A secondary income source outside your primary job, often providing income for aggressive saving.
terms.more: Dramatically accelerates wealth building; compresses timeline to goals.

terms.plain: Money earned with minimal ongoing effort, like dividends, rent, or royalties.
terms.more: Build passive income streams to reduce dependence on active work.

terms.plain: Deliberately selling investments at a loss to offset capital gains, reducing tax burden.
terms.more: A free tax reduction strategy; essential for taxable investment accounts.

terms.plain: Direct transfer of IRA funds to charity, counting toward charitable giving without increasing taxable income.
terms.more: Available at 70.5+; maximizes tax efficiency of giving.

terms.plain: A comprehensive roadmap covering goals, cash flow, debt, investments, insurance, and retirement.
terms.more: Written plans dramatically increase success rates vs. vague intentions.

terms.plain: Testing your financial plan against different future scenarios (job loss, market crash, inheritance).
terms.more: Reveals gaps and builds confidence in your resilience.
